append.text: **Ps 10:2 — a cost of *vós* found:** *quómodo dícitis ánimæ meæ* (the advisers, plural) in a psalm that turns to God in 10:4 (*perfecísti*, singular): the Latin tells the two apart by number, Portuguese cannot. *como dizeis à minha alma* was heard by the blind reader FIRST as said to the Lord; *como dizeis vós* (the subject named, set against *o Senhor* of the first colon — D2 allows it) was heard as said to others. The same remedy may serve wherever plural men are addressed next to God (cf. D25 on 7:13).
Ps 10:2 *No Senhor confio* (the Latin's order; MS1932 has the same words); 24:1 *in te confído* is the other place of the form.

**Ps 10:3 *intendérunt arcum* → *armaram o arco*** (no possessive: the Latin has none); passed the Latinist twice and both blind readings. **63:4 *intendérunt arcum rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis* is the twin of 10:3 and should copy *armaram o arco … para flecharem*.**
Ps 10:3 *prepararam as suas setas na aljava*; the verb *sagittáre* is *flechar* (row), so the Latin's echo *sagíttas … sagíttent* is not heard — *assetear* would keep it and is an option in Ps 10.

**Ps 10:4, the place this row was tried on:** *Porque destruíram o que aperfeiçoastes* — natural order (the Latin's object-first *o que aperfeiçoastes, eles destruíram* is the option); the Latinist passed it twice, the blind reader heard 'what the Lord perfected' both times; the stylist named 10:4 the psalm's best line. MS1932 *o que fizeste de bom* refused (a gloss).

Ps 10:7 *Fará chover laços sobre os pecadores*: one blind reading heard snares first, the second heard 'rope loops falling from the sky' without the sense of a trap — kept (the Latin's image; *armadilhas* would explain).
Ps 10:8 *o seu rosto viu a equidade*: listed as unknown by the blind reader twice more; kept.

terms: | passer | pardal (*como um pardal*) | open | Ps 10:2 *Muda-te para o monte como um pardal?*; στρουθίον; 5 verses (grep: 10:2, 83:4 *passer invénit sibi domum*, 101:8 *sicut passer solitárius in tecto*, 103:16 *pásseres*, 123:7a *Ánima nostra sicut passer erépta est de láqueo*) — the named small bird serves all five; DRB *sparrow*; MS1932 *a ave* (generic) is the option. No reader remarked |

| transmigráre | mudar-se (*Muda-te para o monte*) | open | Ps 10:2 only (grep); L&S "remove from one place to another, migrate", Greek μεταναστεύου "change your dwelling". MS1932 and DM1962 *Foge* interpret (flight); options *Migra* (the root; the bird's verb), *Passa*. Passed the Latinist twice, no remark from the stylist or the blind reader |
| pháretra | aljava | working | Ps 10:3 only (grep); the one word for a quiver (MS1932); listed as unknown by the blind reader twice, kept |

| sagittáre | flechar (*para flecharem no escuro os retos de coração*) | open | Ps 10:3, 63:4 (L&S cite both). Transitive, as the Latin; the plain Brazilian verb. Cost: *setas* (sagítta) and *flechar* are two roots, so *sagíttas … sagíttent* (10:3) is not heard as an echo — option *assetear* keeps it but is hardly said in Brazil; MS1932 *disparar contra*. Passed all readers |

| respícere (in) | *estar voltado para* (10:5b *Os seus olhos estão voltados para o pobre*) | open | Ps 10:5b. Draft 1 had *olham para* (MS1932); the stylist refused *os olhos olham* (a jingle the Latin does not have) and gave *estão voltados para* — a participle of state, not the reflexive *voltar-se* that is *convértere*'s (6:5); it lets the re- be heard; the Latinist passed it. The imperative *réspice* (12:3; ἐπίβλεψον, the verb of 118:132 *Áspice in me* → *Olhai para mim*) is decided in Ps 12. 24 verses have the verb (grep); *réspice in me* 21:2, 24:16, 68:17, 85:16. **83:10 *áspice, Deus: et réspice in fáciem Christi tui* sets the two verbs side by side** (ἴδε / ἐπίβλεψον) and must decide locally. **9:30a has the same first colon as 10:5b word for word** (see Formulas) |
| pálpebræ | pálpebras | working | Ps 10:5b *as suas pálpebras interrogam os filhos dos homens* — the concrete image (rule 5); 131:4. The blind reader heard 'the gaze examines' first |

| interrogáre | interrogar (*as suas pálpebras interrogam … O Senhor interroga o justo e o ímpio*) | open | Ps 10:5b, 10:6 — one verb twice, as the Latin and the Greek (ἐξετάζει twice). L&S: to question; "to interrogate judicially, to examine" — the judge's scene of 10:5–6. DRB *examine … trieth*, MS1932 *examinam … sonda*; *examinar* is the option; *sondar* is scrutári's (7:10). Heard by the blind reader as 'asks questions, demands an account' first, 'tests' second. Other places 34:11, 136:3a *interrogavérunt nos … verba cantiónum*, 138:23 *intérroga me* (grep) — *interrogai-me* is safe at the imperative (past *interroguei*) |

| plúere (transitive) | fazer chover (*Fará chover laços sobre os pecadores*) | working | Ps 10:7 (MS1932); 77:24 *pluit illis manna*, 77:27. Bare *Choverá laços* is heard as impersonal and loses the subject |

| spíritus procellárum | vento de tempestades | open | Ps 10:7 *fogo e enxofre e vento de tempestades* (bare, as the Latin list); πνεῦμα καταιγίδος; **148:8 *Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum* — another bare list — should copy it**. *espírito* is never wind in Portuguese; options *o sopro das tempestades*, MS1932 *tempestades* (drops spíritus) |

| calix / pars | cálice / parte (*são a parte do cálice deles*) | working | Ps 10:7; 15:5 *pars hereditátis meæ et cálicis mei*, 22:5, 74:8, 115:4 *Cálicem salutáris*. *Cálice* is a proparoxytone: at a cadence it wants a word after it (10:7 *do cálice deles*, which also keeps *seu* from being heard as God's). *pórtio* keeps *porção*. The blind reader heard the cup's sense — the lot of punishment — at once |

| justítiæ (plural) | as justiças (*e amou as justiças*) | open | Ps 10:8, where the Greek is δικαιοσύνας (plural of δικαιοσύνη); DRB and MS1932 make it singular. Heard by one blind reading as 'just acts', by another as 'justice as a quality' — never as the courts, which was the risk. The other plurals (17:23, 49:16, 74:3, 88:32, 147:8 — grep) are in several places δικαιώματα and should decide locally (*preceitos* may be wanted) |

| vultus | rosto (*o seu rosto viu a equidade*) | working | Ps 4:7 *a luz do vosso rosto*, Ps 10:8 (the Latin's reading — his face saw equity — not the Hebrew's 'the upright shall see his face'); keeps *face* for fácies |

| sedes (God's) | trono (*o Senhor tem no céu o seu trono*) | working | Ps 10:5a (θρόνος); *sede* is headquarters or thirst. In 10:5a the Latin's anaphora *Dóminus … Dóminus* is kept and a verb supplied (*tem*) for the hanging nominative; MS1932 *o trono do Senhor está no céu* is the option. 44:7 *Sedes tua, Deus*, 88:15, 92:2, 102:19 |
formulas: | *Óculi ejus in páuperem respíciunt* (9:30a = 10:5b, first colon, word for word; 65:7 *óculi ejus super gentes respíciunt* is near) | *Os seus olhos estão voltados para o pobre* | open — Ps 10 (the stylist's, for draft 1 *olham para*; Latinist clean). **Ps 9 and Ps 10 were translated at the same time by two agents: whichever wording is ruled, the two must be made identical** (in 9:30a the eyes are the sinner's, in 10:5b the Lord's — the words are the same) |

| *intendérunt arcum … ut sagíttent* (10:3; 63:4 *intendérunt arcum rem amáram, ut sagíttent in occúltis immaculátum*) | *armaram o arco … para flecharem* | open — Ps 10; **Ps 63 copies it** (hangs on *sagittáre*) |
